routes.reason: New roadmap QuantitativeOrbitMethodAndMicrolocalAnalysisOnLieGroups for the paper's local machinery, taking 74 of the 92 missing items. The claim that nothing in the atlas goes in this direction survives checking: no layer title or description in data/atlas.json contains 'orbit method', 'Kirillov', 'microlocal', 'coadjoint', 'Plancherel' or 'relative character'. The alternative of a Part II of the Tau Ceti representation-theory family is excluded by that family's own README, which the reason quotes accurately — 'no representations of noncompact groups, no Plancherel theory, no tempered spectrum … their unitary duals are not [in scope]'. The area 'representations' is a galaxy id, and the 515-word brief states the final theorems in the published numbering (4.5, 5.6, 5.8, 7.4, 8.11, 6.1, 6.3, 12.2, 11.1, 14.2, 14.5, 16.7, 17.2, 19.3, 22.2, 24.5, 26.4–26.5, 27.1, 27.7, 29.1, 30.1) with the order to cover them in, which is what a design job needs. It also says which parts are the reusable core, so a reviewer of the design job can split Parts I–II from III–V.

New roadmap GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups for the 18 automorphic items. This is the right shape: the roadmap is already proposed by six other extractions (PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22, PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-25, PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22 and PAPER-MAO-WAN-ZHANG-26), and I checked that all of them use exactly this id, this title and the area 'automorphic', so the design job will receive one coherent proposal rather than competing ones. Nothing in the atlas plans it: no layer mentions Gan–Gross–Prasad, Ichino or Bessel models. The brief adds what this paper contributes rather than restating the others — the k1-form of GGP pairs, the eigenvalue invariants and stability versus conductor dropping, positivity and non-vanishing of relative characters, the branching coefficient L(Π, Σ), the Ichino–Ikeda/N. Harris conjecture as a conjecture, and Theorem 31.11 with its hypotheses, family size and weak subconvexity.

notes: Accept. 99 items over a 209-page paper, 3 library, 4 planned and 92 missing, every missing item routed exactly once. I reproduced both hashes the source block records (published 85e14654…, arXiv v3 9bce49cb…). The published Acta PDF is permission-flagged, so it was read as a PDF reader reads it; with the text in hand, all 88 locator checks pass — 82 land on exactly the page given and the other six are locators that name a proof or a passage following a statement, each confirmed by reading the page (Theorem 27.7 stated on p. 183 with its proof on 184–185; Lemma 27.3 on 181 with the proof on 182; Lemma 7.6 on 48, proof on 49; Lemma 19.5 on 129, proof on 130; Definition 4.3 on 33 with the passage after it on 34; Lemma 10.4 on 81, proof on 82). Both routes are new roadmaps and both are justified — see the route reasons; the two areas are galaxy ids and neither roadmap id exists in the atlas. The four planned items name layers that exist. Of the 15 sourceIssues I checked the one that reaches a stated result and six others verbatim: E1 is right and it matters — p. 182 does argue 'the surjectivity of the spinor norm on SO_{n−1} (for n − 1 ⩾ 2)', §25.7(2) does allow (SO_{n+1}, SO_n) with n ⩾ 2, and for an anisotropic binary form the spinor norm image is the norm group of index 2, so the reduction of Theorem 27.1 through Lemma 27.3 fails for (SO_3, SO_2); the finding's partial repair for Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ) is stated as partial. E2's ∆-identity, E4's display (7.4), E8's C_c^∞(g), E9's ⟨ξ⟩^{m−α} in the h^η S^m_δ display (against the correct ⟨ξ⟩^{m−|α|} of (4.8) just above it), E11's '§5.5' and E14's π(f) := ∫ π(f)f(g) dg are all printed exactly as quoted. One correction was made in place: the library item on Schwartz spaces cited mathlib:SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLE, which does not exist at the pinned commit — the name occurs only in the module docstring of Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzSpace/Fourier.lean. The inversion the item needs is there under other names, so the item stays library with SchwartzMap.instFourierTransform and Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq cited instead. Nothing was rejected and no item was deleted.
